summary: The document provides a high-level functional overview of a Hospital Management System (HMS), listing core modules (EMR, Billing, Pharmacy, etc.) and a generic tech stack (React, FastAPI, PostgreSQL). However, it lacks specific technical specifications, compliance details (HIPAA/GDPR), data models, API contracts, and non-functional performance benchmarks. It is currently a conceptual outline rather than an engineering-ready requirements specification.

risk_factors.title: Lack of Specific PHI Encryption Standards
risk_factors.description: The document mentions 'password encryption' and 'privacy of medical information' but does not specify AES-256 for data at rest or TLS 1.2+ for data in transit, which are mandatory for HIPAA compliance.
risk_factors.mitigation: Explicitly mandate AES-256-GCM for all PHI stored in the database and Redis, and enforce TLS 1.3 for all API communications.

verification.claim: Risk: Lack of Specific PHI Encryption Standards — The document mentions 'password encryption' and 'privacy of medical information' but does not specify AES-256 for data at rest or TLS 1.2+ for data in transit, which are mandatory for HIPAA compliance.
verification.reason: Source mentions encryption but no specific PHI standards.

risk_factors.title: Ambiguous Audit Log Immutability
risk_factors.description: The document lists 'audit logs' as a feature but does not specify immutability, retention periods, or tamper-evidence, which are critical for healthcare regulatory compliance.
risk_factors.mitigation: Define audit logs as append-only, stored in a separate, access-restricted database or WORM (Write Once Read Many) storage, with cryptographic hashing to ensure integrity.

verification.claim: Risk: Ambiguous Audit Log Immutability — The document lists 'audit logs' as a feature but does not specify immutability, retention periods, or tamper-evidence, which are critical for healthcare regulatory compliance.
verification.reason: Audit logs are listed without immutability or retention details.

risk_factors.title: Missing Interoperability Standards (HL7 FHIR/DICOM)
risk_factors.description: The system includes Laboratory and EMR modules but does not mention HL7 FHIR or DICOM standards, which are essential for interoperability with external labs and imaging systems.
risk_factors.mitigation: Specify that the Laboratory module must support HL7 FHIR R4 resources for test orders and results, and the Imaging module (if applicable) must support DICOM 3.0.

verification.claim: Risk: Missing Interoperability Standards (HL7 FHIR/DICOM) — The system includes Laboratory and EMR modules but does not mention HL7 FHIR or DICOM standards, which are essential for interoperability with external labs and imaging systems.
verification.reason: No HL7 FHIR or DICOM references despite lab/EMR modules.

risk_factors.title: Undefined Disaster Recovery Metrics
risk_factors.description: The document mentions 'backup/recovery' but does not define RTO (Recovery Time Objective) or RPO (Recovery Point Objective), which are critical for high-availability healthcare systems.
risk_factors.mitigation: Define RTO < 1 hour and RPO < 5 minutes for critical patient data, with automated failover mechanisms for the database and application servers.

verification.claim: Risk: Undefined Disaster Recovery Metrics — The document mentions 'backup/recovery' but does not define RTO (Recovery Time Objective) or RPO (Recovery Point Objective), which are critical for high-availability healthcare systems.
verification.reason: Backup/recovery is mentioned without RTO/RPO metrics.

risk_factors.title: Generic Authentication Without MFA
risk_factors.description: The document mentions 'JWT/OAuth-based authentication' but does not specify Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for privileged roles (Admin, Doctor), which is a HIPAA best practice.
risk_factors.mitigation: Require MFA for all staff roles, especially Admin and Doctor, using TOTP or WebAuthn.

verification.claim: Risk: Generic Authentication Without MFA — The document mentions 'JWT/OAuth-based authentication' but does not specify Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for privileged roles (Admin, Doctor), which is a HIPAA best practice.
verification.reason: Authentication described without MFA for privileged roles.

conflicts_and_ambiguities.context: Non-functional requirements should include... high availability
conflicts_and_ambiguities.suggested_resolution: Define high availability as 99.9% uptime with automated failover, and specify the maximum allowable downtime for critical services.

verification.claim: Ambiguity: Vague 'High Availability' Definition — Non-functional requirements should include... high availability
verification.reason: High availability is cited without definition or metrics.

conflicts_and_ambiguities.issue: Unclear Data Ownership and GDPR Compliance
conflicts_and_ambiguities.suggested_resolution: Specify GDPR compliance if EU patients are involved, including data subject rights (access, erasure, portability) and data residency requirements.

verification.reason: Privacy is mentioned but data ownership and GDPR specifics are missing.

conflicts_and_ambiguities.suggested_resolution: Define specific latency benchmarks, e.g., 95th percentile API response time < 200ms for read operations and < 500ms for write operations.

verification.reason: Fast API responses are noted without measurable criteria.
